title: Song of Solomon Bible Quiz - Chapter 1
description: Ten questions on Song of Solomon 1: the song which is Solomon's, love better than wine, the vineyards of En Gedi, and eyes like doves.

questions.text: Whose song is the Song of songs, according to the first verse?
questions.explanation: The opening verse says it is the Song of songs, which is Solomon's.

questions.text: What does the speaker say the beloved's love is better than?
questions.explanation: She says, "Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your love is better than wine."

questions.text: The speaker says she is dark but lovely. To what does she compare herself?
questions.explanation: She tells the daughters of Jerusalem she is dark but lovely, like Kedar's tents, like Solomon's curtains.

answers.text: The cedars of Lebanon and the firs

questions.text: Why does the speaker say she is dark?
questions.explanation: She says, "Don't stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me."

answers.text: Because she was born in Kedar
Because she works in the king's kitchens
Because the sun has scorched her

questions.text: What did her mother's sons, who were angry with her, make her do?
questions.explanation: Her mother's sons were angry with her and made her keeper of the vineyards, but she has not kept her own vineyard.

answers.text: They made her graze the young goats
They made her keeper of the vineyards
They made her serve at the king's table
They made her draw water at noon

questions.text: To what does the beloved compare his love in verse 9?
questions.explanation: He says, "I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh's chariots."

answers.text: A dove in the clefts of the rock

questions.text: The speaker calls her beloved a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of which place?
questions.explanation: She says, "My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi."

questions.text: What does the beloved say her eyes are like?
questions.explanation: He says, "Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Your eyes are like doves."

questions.text: When did the speaker's perfume spread its fragrance?
questions.explanation: She says, "While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance."

answers.text: While the king sat at his table

questions.text: What are the beams of their house, according to the last verse?
questions.explanation: The chapter ends, "The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs."
